evidence: Frozen file hashes match the manifest (task.toml 15b097b6..., test.sh bd682592..., functional judge.toml bc2a7954..., polish 189df547..., visual dde89eef..., render 84fe3268..., constraints ec368d99...). Arithmetic (nesting half - holds): task.toml [agent].timeout_sec = 7200.0, [environment].build_timeout_sec = 600.0, [verifier].timeout_sec = 13200.0 (all equal to the template). test.sh:207 runs every suite with 'timeout $budget_sec rewardkit --max-concurrent-agent 1', so judges within a suite run serially; test.sh:213 gates budget 1500, test.sh:224 scored budget 11100 (template values). Gates: render timeout 600 + constraints timeout 600 (both batched) = 1200 < 1500 (300 s slack). Scored: functional judge.toml:6,12 mode = "individual", timeout = 550; rewardkit 0.1.7 judges.py:467-494 (_arun_agent_individual) grades each criterion in its own sequential agent call and judges.py:538-549 applies asyncio.wait_for(timeout=judge.timeout) per call, so 550 is per criterion. 16 criteria (counted with tomllib) x 550 = 8800; + polish 900 (batched) + visual 900 (batched) = 10600 < 11100 (500 s slack), matching the comment at functional judge.toml:7-11. Verifier: 1500 + 11100 = 12600 < 13200; sum of all judge timeouts 1200 + 10600 = 11800 < 13200 (internal annotation). The remaining 600 s covers liveness (test.sh:115-122, 120 x 0.25 s plus up to 2 x 2 s urlopen per probe, worst case about 510 s for a hung-but-accepting app), the /app copy, prompt substitution and two score.py runs. The persistence criterion's restart helper (30 s readiness loop, 55 s MCP timeout per staged-task-contract.md) runs inside its 550 s criterion. Each judge timeout is below its own suite budget (600 < 1500; 550, 900, 900 < 11100). Sufficiency half (not measured): the template ships functional as batched/9000 (rules/projects/webdev-task-template/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:3-4); this task switched to individual/550, and the task's own comment (functional judge.toml:10-11) says 'individual mode is the lead's instruction, relayed by the task owner on 8 Oct 2026. Not yet measured against a judge run.' The suite budgets themselves are unchanged, so no timeout increase needed authorization. raw-evidence-index.json scope states 'Full configured grading/workload ... are absent' and the only runtime evidence is a scripted Playwright golden run (golden-run.log 21:52:33Z-21:54:13Z, all 16 functional checks PASS in ~100 s total), which is explicitly 'Not a configured judge run ... or judge-duration measurement'. Under REVIEW_POLICY ('Workload is measured, not inferred from a timeout number') and SKILL.md ('Never upgrade an unmeasured claim to Pass'), whether 550 s is long enough for a z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx claude-code judge driving Playwright MCP per criterion is unmeasured. The heaviest criteria are plausibly tight: deleted_and_expired_messages (weight 3.0, 1969-char description) needs sign-ins as gwen, harriet and sian, posting, replying, deleting, recording and replaying a delete request, several searches, a transcript check and a Part B boundary check; persistence (weight 2.0) does about 10 setup actions across two users, restart_app, a fresh sign-in, and around 10 readbacks plus cleanup; search_and_transcript (2.5) and hold_scope_and_release (2.0) are similar multi-user flows. Each individual session also pays a fresh claude-code start, a fresh --isolated browser and a fresh sign-in. Latent harness note (template-wide, not a task defect): judges.py:229 _MAX_JUDGE_RETRIES = 3 retries schema-mismatch responses, each with a fresh full timeout, so worst-case wall time can exceed the nominal sums (3 x 550 per criterion); a scored-suite overrun makes test.sh:224-225 exit with score.py's gates-stage record (scored dimensions 0, reward 0). Template batched/9000 has the same exposure.
counterexample: Conforming app graded wrongly (plausible, unmeasured): the golden app is correct, but the flash judge needs about 40-60 Playwright MCP turns for deleted_and_expired_messages (three accounts, a recorded-request replay, searches, a transcript and the seven-day boundary). At roughly 10-15 s per turn this takes more than 550 s. judges.py:542-549 then records the criterion as 0.0 ('judge timed out after 550s'), costing 3.0/33 functional weight. The Oracle would fall below 1.0 even though the app is correct. Broken app: timeouts do not let a broken app pass; a timed-out criterion scores 0, so this row's risk is only false negatives.
suggested_fix: Before declaring the task ready, run one full configured verifier pass on the golden app, with existing authorization for provider spend. Record each functional criterion's wall time from rewardkit.log and the per-criterion warnings, and confirm that none times out and that each has comfortable headroom (for example, at most about 70% of 550 s). If any criterion runs tight, trim or split its steps, or rebalance within the unchanged 11100 s budget (for example, lower polish or visual from 900 s if measurements show they finish well under it). Do not raise the budgets automatically; a raise needs a recorded reason and authorization, staying below five hours.
